# AquaSentinel

> A virtual water-quality sensor estimating E. coli risk (Safe/Unsafe) for the Center City
> tidal Delaware from live USGS gauge and weather data. This is an estimate, not a measured
> bacteria value - language stays to "estimate" and "flag elevated risk," and never claims
> to forecast human health outcomes.

AquaSentinel publishes its live scored reading through three agent-facing surfaces, all
generated from the same scoring output so they cannot disagree with each other or the
human-facing dashboard:

- [MCP server](/mcp) - read-only tools: list_monitored_locations, get_current_status,
  get_recent_readings. No write tools exist - an agent can read status, never change
  anything.
- [Status endpoint](/api/status) - the same data as a plain JSON GET, no MCP client needed.
- [Methodology](https://github.com/gouriprakash-spec/aquasentinel/blob/main/docs/product-brief.md) - the full design:
  data sources, model, alert rules, and honesty guardrails.

How the status is decided (by deterministic code, never by an agent):
- Safe/Unsafe comes from a disclosed rainfall rule: Unsafe when rain over the two previous
  calendar days is at least 2.5 mm. A nearby combined-sewer overflow reported by CSOCast can also
  force Unsafe; that check can only raise the status, never lower it.
- Live USGS gauge readings (turbidity, temperature, conductance, dissolved oxygen, pH) feed a
  model trained on past near-shore E. coli samples. The model never decides the status; it only
  produces `confidence`, the agreement between the rule and the model. When the gauge has no
  current reading, `confidence` and the water-quality values are null: read them as "not
  available", never as zero. The status itself is still given.

Every reading is an estimate that flags elevated risk of exceeding the EPA 235 CFU/100mL
single-sample E. coli threshold - never a measured bacteria value.
